reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Bio: Mario Garza is the artist and researcher behind Symbolic Studies, a project sharing symbolic insights on the zodiac, mythology, folklore and world religions, with astrology as its foundation. A lifelong artist who has worked as an art director and graphic designer for nearly 25 years, he runs Symbolic Studies from the Pacific Northwest alongside his wife Michelle, who co-hosts the podcast with him. His work traces syncretic threads across tarot, occultism and comparative religion, including the argument that the major deities of antiquity were originally polar gods before a solar model was laid over them. He also offers symbolic birth chart and tarot readings, private lessons and freelance design.
reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Name: Mario Garza

recl1wvjyRP3XfBBu.Bio: Marty Leeds is a gematria researcher, author and preacher who founded The Gnostic Church and Academy of Lord Jesus Christ in 2022, where he serves as head teacher and spiritual leader. A working minister since 2011, he is the author of more than ten books, among them the Pi & The English Alphabet series, Scripture in the Stars, The Keys to the Tarot and Gnosticism Defined: The Tenets of The Order, built around a mathematical cipher he says is hidden beneath the English alphabet. His teaching centers on Prisca Theologia, the idea of a single wisdom underlying the world's religions, drawing together gematria, Kabbalah, astrology and comparative mythology. He streams weekly sermons free through the Gnostic Academy's YouTube and Rumble channels.
recl1wvjyRP3XfBBu.Name: Marty Leeds

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Sacred Math and the Septenary Cipher", "body": "Marty Leeds walks through the septenary cipher, his seven based gematria system, showing how the word seven itself hides the numbers seven and twenty two, the classic fraction for approximating pi. He ties that into the tarot's structure: twenty two Major Arcana cards, fifty six Minor Arcana split into four suits of fourteen, mirroring the fourteen phalanges on a hand, for seventy eight cards total, which also equals one through twelve summed, the twelve houses of astrology. Even earth, air, water and fire, the elements of the astrological wheel, sum to seventy eight again, reinforcing what he calls a self referential, mathematically encoded system, not coincidence."}, {"title": "The Fool, the Magician and the Holy Fool", "body": "Mario reads the Fool and Magician as chaos becoming order, echoing the primordial jumble of elements in Ovid's Metamorphoses before a world axis separates heaven from earth. Marty adds that Genesis performs the same split, with earth, air, water and fire present before God says let there be light, a phrase whose gematria equals seventy two, the same value as Lord Jesus Christ. The Fool sums to thirty, but adding holy brings it to forty two, the Magician's number, and Marty notes those same digits begin the unfolding of pi, three one four. Even the Fool's own divisors, he says, reduce mathematically straight to Lord Jesus Christ."}, {"title": "Stars and Constellations Hidden in the Cards", "body": "Several cards double as star charts for the two guests. The Chariot's motionless charioteer is an unmoved mover whose wheels sit in the waters of heaven, which Marty links to the constellation Auriga while Mario traces the glyph for seven to the seven stars of Ursa Major wheeling around the pole. The Hermit stands atop a world mountain, his lantern and closed eyes pointing toward Polaris, with Mario connecting the card's Virgo rulership to Mercury. Marty argues the Fool himself is Orion, walking obliviously toward a ledge while Canis Major, the barking dog, marks Sirius, the star that signals where the sun rises each December twenty fifth."}, {"title": "Mercury, the World Axis and Sacred Geometry", "body": "Mercury keeps resurfacing as the one planet with no zodiacal opposite, which Marty reads as its role uniting opposites, the alchemical coincidentia oppositorum; its eighty eight day orbit divided by twenty eight phalanges of the hand approximates pi again. Mario frames Mercury, the Hermit's staff and the Magician's raised and lowered hands as the same Axis Mundi, the spinal column and world pillar connecting above and below. That geometry resolves into the cube, Marty's stand in for Kabbalah, with Jesus and the Magician reducing through gematria to four thirty two, doubling to four thousand three twenty, the degrees of two cubes, alongside the six six six drawn from Jesus's value."}, {"title": "The Fool's Journey as Human Awakening", "body": "Beyond the numbers, both guests treat the Fool as everyman, someone who, like the rest of us, simply hasn't recognized his own divine spark yet. Chance frames it as all people being peepholes of God, each ego a temporary window onto something infinite. Mario reads the Fool's eagle topped bag as Scorpio's sexual energy, either weighing him down or transformed, Phoenix like, into enlightenment, noting he's the only figure in the deck shown walking, traveling lightly rather than burdened. Chance shares his own experience of choosing, during mystical states, to return to ordinary life, framing the Fool's descent from the mountain as a forgetting on the road back to wholeness."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Is the tarot a system of sacred mathematics hiding in plain sight? Marty Leeds of the Gnostic Academy and Mario Garza of Symbolic Studies join Chance Garton to unpack the numerical architecture Marty lays out in his new book, The Keys to the Tarot. Working from septenary gematria, sacred geometry and astrotheology, the three trace how seventy eight cards, twenty two Major Arcana and the recurring approximation of pi turn a deck of cards into what Marty calls a self referential, deliberately encoded system.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: From there the conversation opens into the Fool and the Magician, Mercury as the axis that unites opposites, Orion hidden inside the Hermit and the Chariot, and the tarot read as a pictorial map of the soul's own hero's journey through incarnation and awakening.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Ophiuchus and the Exit from the Wheel", "body": "Marty Leeds maps the Major Arcana as a crossing of the Milky Way from Orion, the one constellation anyone can point out, to Ophiuchus the serpent holder, who neither kills nor beheads the snake but masters it while standing on Scorpio, the conquered animal state. You are reborn through his body the way Jesus is reborn from the sealed tomb once the stone is rolled away. Chance Garton and Mario Garza refuse Ophiuchus as a literal thirteenth sign, noting how cleanly a circle divides into twelve and how badly into thirteen, and read him instead as the step off the wheel of fortune, echoed by the ouroboros on the Magician's belt."}, {"title": "The High Priestess at the Silver Gate", "body": "Her name totals ninety in the septenary cipher, the square and the right angle pointing down into matter and mother, while her twin pillars read as a gateway, the Gemini glyph ruled by lunar Mercury, with the crescent moon at her feet. Marty Leeds sets her at the Silver Gate, where the Milky Way crosses the ecliptic between Gemini and Taurus: bull horns on her head, her robe the white river pouring through, the moon beneath her the silver itself. Mario Garza puts Daath, the hidden eleventh sephiroth, at her head, crossed by gimel, the camel that carries the seeker over the abyss; triangulating to eleven gives sixty six, and sixty six over twenty one yields pi."}, {"title": "Thrones, the Kaaba and the Two Mothers", "body": "Mario Garza notes the High Priestess opens a run of throned figures through the Empress, Emperor and Hierophant, broken only when the Lovers stand, arguing the throne belonged first to the goddess, receptive rather than projective, like Isis enthroned with Horus; Cassiopeia sits in the stars on what looks less a chair than the white cube of the Kaaba, veiled by its kiswah, house of the mother. He takes the Empress as terrestrial mother to the spiritual one, wheat for Virgo, twelve stars for the zodiac. Marty Leeds makes it arithmetic: the vesica piscis holds the square root of three, the measure hidden inside a cube, and the Empress totals forty nine, seven times seven."}, {"title": "Seven, the Virgin Number, and the World Mountain", "body": "Marty Leeds calls seven a virgin number: nothing in the decad multiplies up into it. One through seven gives five thousand forty, and so does seven through ten, the figure used to proportion the squared circle; every digit divides three hundred sixty evenly except seven, and the word seven totals twenty two, pi's numerator, which he takes as proof a creator works through language. Mario Garza ties seven to the alchemical stages and the Hermit's Virgo retreat, then reads the Emperor, on a silver throne, as Mount Meru with four rivers from the pole, citing Rene Guenon's The King of the World. Marty derives forty four from the Masonic compass at forty seven degrees against the square at ninety."}, {"title": "Forty Three, the Counted Rays and the Central Sun", "body": "Chance Garton walks the lattice into the pictures. The Hierophant totals fifty nine, matching Jesus Christ and alchemical wedding, so the thrones restate the union of opposites, until the Lovers step off them at forty three, Adam and Eve as that union in one card. Only two Major Arcana suns carry black line rays; counted three times over, they give forty three on the Lovers and fourteen on the Fool, and forty four over fourteen approximates pi. Mario Garza reads the Fool's shortest seventh ray as the pole extended, citing Guenon on an invisible seventh color, and calls these the central or philosopher's sun. Chance closes on the skull: twenty two bones, seven orifices, sutures that dismember and remember."}]

It encodes many, many secrets, what symbols represent, what numbers represent, what these cards represent.", "author": "Mario Garza", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/94a2fe35-cc60-4591-8931-7e2b7af18c82/MARIO-GARZA.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "This is clearly encoded, there's no way that this stuff is random because it's all self-referential.", "author": "Marty Leeds", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/9317d892-142f-40f7-9891-729784cb3655/MARTY-LEEDS.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I think you get the glyph for the number seven, how we actually draw number seven from Ursa Major.", "author": "Mario Garza", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/94a2fe35-cc60-4591-8931-7e2b7af18c82/MARIO-GARZA.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The combination of major and minor cards in the whole deck is seventy-eight.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Mercury represents the transcension of those opposites, which is the core of alchemy.", "author": "Marty Leeds", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/9317d892-142f-40f7-9891-729784cb3655/MARTY-LEEDS.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The fact that the fool's pole is pointing directly to the sun.", "author": "Mario Garza", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/94a2fe35-cc60-4591-8931-7e2b7af18c82/MARIO-GARZA.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "We're all the fool, but we're all people.
